questions.question: What is the difference between mutable and immutable objects in Python?
questions.title: Mutable vs Immutable Objects in Python
questions.direct_answer: Mutable objects can change in place, such as list, dict, and set. Immutable objects cannot change after creation, such as int, float, bool, str, tuple, and frozenset; an apparent change creates a new object. Variables are names bound to objects, not typed boxes.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you understand references, in-place updates, and function side effects.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Calling a variable itself mutable or assuming tuple contents are always deeply immutable.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Explain that a tuple is immutable as a container but may contain a mutable list.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Define Mutable vs Immutable Objects in Python simply, show a small example, and mention the main trade-off or edge case.

sections.title: Names point to objects
sections.content: Python variables hold references to objects. A mutable object can be updated without changing its identity; an immutable value must be replaced.

sections.title: In-place versus replacement
sections.content:
```python
a = [1, 2]
b = a
a.append(3)   # b sees [1, 2, 3]

x = 1
y = x
x += 1       # creates a new integer object
```

sections.title: Interview cues
items: Lists, dicts, and sets are mutable.
Strings, numbers, bools, and tuples are immutable containers.
Use a copy when a function must not mutate a caller's collection.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content: Python names refer to objects. Mutable objects like lists and dictionaries can change in place, so aliases observe that change. Immutable objects like strings and integers cannot change; operations create a new object.
